issues.legal_issue: A dying declaration recorded by a police officer is admissible, but should ordinarily be avoided when a better method of recording it is available.
material_facts: An investigating police officer recorded a wounded person's statement during the investigation.
The court found that no other person was available in the village to record that statement because the wounded person was in a critical condition.
Other declarations recorded by police were not relied upon, and the court also found reasons to doubt what those declarations said.
issues.conclusion: A police-recorded dying declaration is not inadmissible merely because a police officer recorded it, but the practice should not be encouraged; it may be relied upon when there was no time or facility to use a better method.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32 of the Indian Evidence Act makes a dying declaration admissible, subject to the exception in Section 162(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Relying on Munnu Raja and Anr. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the court said that an investigating officer should not ordinarily record such a declaration and that the prosecution should explain why a Magistrate or doctor did not record it; a police-recorded declaration may be relied upon if no better method was available.

predicates.criminal_trial_or_appeal: The matter is a criminal trial or an appeal arising from one.
predicates.dying_declaration_recorded_by_police: A police officer recorded a statement from a person who later died and whose statement concerned the cause or circumstances of death.
predicates.no_time_or_facility_for_better_recording: There was no time or practical means to have a more reliable person record the statement.

issues.definition: When a police officer records a dying declaration and no better recording method was available, the declaration is not excluded solely because the recorder was a police officer.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for a death cannot stand when the declarations identifying the accused are not relied upon and the remaining evidence does not establish responsibility beyond reasonable doubt.
material_facts: The deceased persons were attacked at a place some distance from the house where the eyewitnesses saw the earlier attacks.
No witness directly saw the appellants attack those deceased persons.
The court found that the statement attributing those deaths to the appellants went beyond what its maker could have known or seen, and the other dying declarations were not relied upon.
After those declarations were left out of consideration, the court found no direct evidence or conclusive chain of circumstantial evidence connecting the appellants to those deaths.
issues.conclusion: The appellants could not legally be held responsible for the two deaths on the evidence available, and their convictions for those murders could not be maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the requirement that criminal responsibility be established by legally sufficient evidence. In the absence of direct evidence or a conclusive chain of circumstantial evidence, the appellants could not be held responsible for these deaths.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and accused_convicted_of_death and identifying_declarations_not_reliable and no_direct_evidence and circumstantial_chain_not_conclusive

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.accused_convicted_of_death: The accused was convicted of causing a particular person's death.
predicates.identifying_declarations_not_reliable: The statements identifying the accused as responsible for the death are not relied upon as reliable evidence.
predicates.no_direct_evidence: No witness directly saw the accused commit the fatal attack.
predicates.circumstantial_chain_not_conclusive: The remaining circumstances do not form a conclusive chain establishing the accused's responsibility for the death.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a conviction for a death, the conviction cannot stand if the identifying declarations are unreliable and neither direct evidence nor a conclusive circumstantial chain establishes responsibility.

issues.legal_issue: Credible injured eyewitness evidence may sustain convictions against some accused even when the witnesses also implicated another accused who was acquitted.
material_facts: Two prosecution witnesses were injured in the occurrence and testified about the attacks they witnessed.
They implicated an additional accused who was acquitted.
The trial court and the High Court believed these witnesses, and the Supreme Court found their account truthful as to the murders supported by their evidence.
issues.conclusion: The witnesses' implication of the acquitted accused did not require rejection of their evidence in its entirety, and their evidence supported maintaining the convictions for the deaths they witnessed.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the credibility and evidentiary value of the witnesses in the circumstances of the case; it did not treat the inclusion of an acquitted person in their account as a reason to discard the whole account.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.injured_eyewitnesses_witnessed_the_offen: Witnesses who were injured in the occurrence directly saw the offence being committed.
predicates.their_account_is_credible: The court finds the witnesses' account truthful and reliable on the material matters supporting the conviction.
predicates.witnesses_also_implicated_an_acquitted_p: The witnesses also named a person who was not ultimately convicted.

issues.definition: Credible evidence from injured eyewitnesses may support conviction of other accused even if those witnesses also implicated someone who was acquitted.

issues.legal_issue: The non-examination of persons who were not eyewitnesses does not undermine the prosecution case merely because a witness had gone to them after the occurrence.
material_facts: Two persons who were not examined were described as persons whom a prosecution witness had approached.
The court found that neither was an eyewitness.
The court found no basis to conclude that their non-examination affected the prosecution case.
issues.conclusion: The non-examination of those persons did not affect the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered the relevance of the unexamined persons to the evidence and held that their absence did not undermine the case because they were not eyewitnesses.

predicates.criminal_trial_or_appeal: The matter is a criminal trial or an appeal arising from one.
predicates.unexamined_person_was_not_an_eyewitness: A person who was not examined did not directly witness the offence.
predicates.no_case_specific_effect_on_prosecution_e: The record does not show that the person's absence otherwise affected the prosecution evidence.

issues.definition: The absence of an unexamined person who was not an eyewitness does not undermine the prosecution case when no effect on the evidence is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A delay of a few hours in the report reaching the local Magistrate does not, by itself, establish that the report was ante-timed or that the prosecution account was false.
material_facts: A report was made to the police post shortly after the occurrence and registered at the police station later that evening.
The local Magistrate received the report a few hours later.
The court rejected the claim that this delay showed the report had been ante-timed and found the eyewitness evidence truthful.
issues.conclusion: The timing objection did not justify rejecting the prosecution case or finding that the report was ante-timed.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the timing objection in light of the evidence and circumstances as a whole and found the delay in receipt by the Magistrate insufficient to support the allegation.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.report_made_and_registered_soon_after_oc: The report was made and registered soon after the occurrence.
predicates.magistrate_received_report_after_a_short: The Magistrate received the report a few hours after it was made or registered.
predicates.credible_evidence_does_not_support_ante_: The credible evidence does not support the allegation that the report was created or dated earlier than it was in fact made.

issues.definition: A short delay in a Magistrate receiving a report made and registered soon after an occurrence does not establish ante-timing when credible evidence does not support that allegation.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence may be commuted to life imprisonment for an accused whose age and lesser established responsibility make that punishment appropriate, even when death sentences are maintained for co-accused.
material_facts: The accused whose sentence was commuted was in his twenties and was a grand-nephew of the deceased family members.
The court could not find, for lack of legal evidence, that he was responsible for two of the five deaths.
The court generally agreed with the reasons given below for imposing the death penalty but considered a more lenient sentence appropriate for this accused.
issues.conclusion: The death sentence for this accused was commuted to life imprisonment, while the death sentences for the other two appellants were maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied individualized sentencing, considering the accused's age and the extent of responsibility established by legally sufficient evidence. It found those considerations justified a more lenient sentence for this accused while leaving the sentences of the other two appellants undisturbed.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_death_sentence and accused_is_young and evidence_does_not_establish_responsibility_for_all_attributed_deaths and individualized_assessment_favors_leniency

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_death_sentence: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a death sentence.
predicates.accused_is_young: The accused was a young adult at the time of the offence.
predicates.evidence_does_not_establish_responsibili: The evidence does not legally establish the accused's responsibility for all the deaths attributed to the group.
predicates.individualized_assessment_favors_lenienc: The court's assessment of the accused's circumstances and established role favors a more lenient sentence.

issues.definition: When a young accused appealing a death sentence is not legally shown to be responsible for all the deaths attributed to the group and an individual assessment favors leniency, the death sentence is commuted to life imprisonment.

issues.legal_issue: A fine need not be imposed in addition to a death sentence when the circumstances do not make a fine necessary.
material_facts: The trial court imposed a separate fine for each murder along with the death sentences.
The Supreme Court concluded that, on the facts of the case, a fine was not necessary after imposing the death sentences.
issues.conclusion: The fines imposed on all three appellants were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that, on the circumstances before it, the death sentences did not need to be accompanied by fines.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_sentence: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a sentence.
predicates.death_sentence_is_imposed: A death sentence has been imposed on the accused.
predicates.circumstances_do_not_make_fine_necessary: The court finds that the circumstances do not require a fine in addition to the death sentence.

issues.definition: If a death sentence is imposed and the circumstances do not require an additional fine, the fine is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: An opportunity to address the sentencing question at trial and in the High Court is sufficient compliance with the requirement of a sentencing hearing.
material_facts: The trial court gave the appellants an opportunity to present arguments on sentence.
Arguments on sentence were also presented in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The court found no infirmity in the sentencing process on this ground.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the opportunity to address sentence before the trial court, together with arguments on sentence in the High Court, sufficiently complied with the applicable requirement.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_sentence: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a sentence.
predicates.opportunity_to_address_sentence_given_at: The accused was given an opportunity to present arguments on sentence at trial.
predicates.sentence_arguments_presented_on_appeal: Arguments on sentence were also presented in the appellate court.

issues.definition: The sentencing hearing requirement is satisfied when the accused had an opportunity to address sentence at trial and sentence arguments were presented on appeal.
